findings.issue_text: Reader thread is not synchronized before deletion, so it may perform zero reads and let the regression test pass without exercising concurrent access
Test asserts caughtExceptions without joining the reader thread, allowing an in-flight failure to be recorded after the assertion passes
Non-daemon reader thread is stopped only on the normal path, so an earlier main-thread exception can leave it running indefinitely and hang the test process

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-daemon reader thread is stopped only on the normal path, so an earlier main-thread exception can leave it running indefinitely and hang the test process

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while `!deletedAll.get()`. If an exception occurs in the main thread before `deletedAll.set(true)` is called (e.g., during group creation or deletion), the reader thread will never terminate because `deletedAll` remains false. The thread is not a daemon thread, so it will prevent the JVM/test process from exiting. This is a real defect in the test code - the thread should be marked as daemon or wrapped in a try-finally to ensure `deletedAll.set(true)` is always called.
